<!-- ## Pre-class prep -->

<!-- No pre-class prep before our first day of class! -->

Today we run a complete data science workflow together, from a data file on the course
website to a finished chart. We're jumping right into this before we learn how all of the individual pieces work to give you a sense of where things are going and the overall structure and rhythm of python and its data science libraries. 

The morning session has two parts. First we meet python in Positron, which is the application we will write every line of code in for duration of the course (and, likely, for much of your year in the MEDS program). The version of Positron we will be using runs in a browser on the Bren server. Then we will cover just enough Python "grammar" to read the afternoon's code: what a variable is, what a string
is, and how to use print statements.

In the afternoon we will analyze a single file of daily Arctic weather, recorded at Toolik Lake in Alaska between June 1988 and December 2018. By the end of the day, you will have imported that file, explored it, grouped it, aggregated it, drawn a chart from it and exported the result. We do not
clean the dataset, because the one column we analyze has no missing values. We will spend Day 4 on cleaning approaches. Some of the afternoon will feel like copy-and-paste and much of it will feel foreign, though you will write one thing yourself: the f-string you learn in the morning session. Today is just an introduction; by the end of the course, you will be able to look back at the commands and tools we use today with familiarity.

## End-of-day practice

Before leaving today, I encourage you to run the same workflow again on your own, changing a few things to see what happens. Nobody expects you to understand every line yet. Today we have learned a valuable skill: reading working code, tinkering with it, and changing it on purpose to achieve a new result. You will use that skill every day for the rest of the course and throughout your data science career.

- [{{< fa pencil title="A pencil" >}} **Day 1 Practice:** Rerun the Workflow](eod-practice/eod-day1-2026.qmd)
